title: A lifted cyclic derived counit represents the native Hom functor
statement:
Let $\mathcal A_X,\mathcal A_Y$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], with additive exact autoequivalences $P,Q$. Put $\mathcal B_X=\mathcal A_X^P$, $\mathcal B_Y=\mathcal A_Y^Q$, the fixed-pair categories [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], and use ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $U_X,U_Y$ for derived forgetting and $\theta$ for the induced action. Let $\mathcal C_X,\mathcal C_Y$ be full subcategories of the bounded ordinary derived categories, closed under isomorphisms and shifts, invariant under $P,Q$ and their inverses. Put $\mathcal W_X=U_X^{-1}(\mathcal C_X)$ and $\mathcal W_Y=U_Y^{-1}(\mathcal C_Y)$ inside the bounded native derived categories.

Let $F:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal C_Y$ and $G:\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_X$ be exact functors with adjunction $F\dashv G$ and counit $\epsilon$. Suppose $a:QF\xrightarrow{\sim}FP$ is a shift-compatible natural isomorphism whose mate $b:PG\xrightarrow{\sim}GQ$ of $a^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] is invertible. Let $F^{\mathrm W}:\mathcal W_X\to\mathcal W_Y$ be exact with a natural shift-compatible comparison $c:U_YF^{\mathrm W}\xrightarrow{\sim}FU_X$ intertwining actions. Assume the natural Hom short exact sequence of [lem-sf-cyclic-derived-hom-exact-sequence] is compatible with $F^{\mathrm W},F,c$ on these subcategories, including the left connecting maps. Explicitly, if $V^r_{K,H}=\operatorname{Hom}(U_XK,U_XH[r])$ and $T^r(u)=\theta_{H[r]}P(u)\theta_K^{-1}$, the sequences are $0\to(V^{-1}_{K,H})_T\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,H)\to(V^0_{K,H})^T\to0$, and similarly on $Y$; $(V)_T=\operatorname{coker}(1-T)$, $(V)^T=\ker(1-T)$. The functor $F^{\mathrm W}$ acts on both outer terms by $F$ under $c$.

For $L\in\mathcal W_Y$ put $N=GU_YL$, $v=G(\theta_L)b_{U_YL}:PN\xrightarrow{\sim}N$. There exist $H_L\in\mathcal W_X$, an action-compatible isomorphism $e_L:U_XH_L\xrightarrow{\sim}N$ satisfying $e_L\theta_{H_L}=vP(e_L)$, and a native derived morphism $d_L:F^{\mathrm W}H_L\to L$ with
$$U_Y(d_L)=\epsilon_{U_YL}F(e_L)c_{H_L}.$$
For every such $H_L,e_L$ and every native lift $d_L$ of the displayed counit, the maps
$$\Psi_K:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal W_X}(K,H_L)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal W_Y}(F^{\mathrm W}K,L),\qquad u\longmapsto d_LF^{\mathrm W}(u)$$
are bijective, naturally in $K$. The maps on degree $-1$ coinvariants and degree $0$ invariants are the bijections induced by the ordinary adjunction in those two degrees, through $e_L,c$ and shift comparisons. No functorial choice of $H_L,e_L,d_L$ is required. The representability includes all native extension morphisms, and does not assume derived forgetting is faithful.

proof.text: Apply cyclic derived action realization to N = G(U(L)) and the invertible action b followed by G(theta_L). Its interval-preservation conclusion gives native boundedness in the same interval, and isomorphism closure of S places the realized H in the required native full subcategory. The induced e satisfies the prescribed action equation.

proof.text: The mate/counit identity for a inverse, counit naturality and naturality of a give a_H followed by F(theta_H), F(e), epsilon equal to Q(F(e) followed by epsilon) followed by theta_L. Compose with c_H and apply its assumed action equation hc. This proves equivariance of the ordinary counit carrier t. Expand the canonical degree-zero shift comparison to see that t followed by the inverse zero-shift identification is in ker(1-T). The surjective map in the assumed native Hom sequence supplies d, and cancellation of the invertible zero-shift map gives exactly U(d)=c_H followed by F(e), epsilon.

proof.text: For every integer r, outerMap is additive and bijective. On ordinary full subcategories equip the right adjoint temporarily with Mathlib Adjunction.rightAdjointCommShift, determined by F and the specified adjunction. Compose the isomorphism Hom(X,Y[r]) to Hom(X,G(Z[r])) induced by shifted e and this shift comparison with the inverse adjunction Hom bijection. Adjunction.shift_counit_app and naturality of the F shift comparison identify its formula with F(u), then the F shift comparison, then the shifted F(e) followed by epsilon. The fully faithful inclusions and their canonical shift isomorphisms identify this bijection with outerMap, including c_K. This construction does not require compatibility of the given shift structure on G with the adjunction.

proof.text: Fix any native lift d with the prescribed underlying carrier. Transport followed by shifted U(d) equals outerMap, since shifted c_H inverse cancels against shifted c_H. Naturality of cyclicDerivedStructure and the derived Q shift comparison show that postcomposition by shifted U(d) commutes with the cyclic action. Together with the action clause of Compatible this proves that outerMap intertwines T in every degree. No shifted mate calculation is needed.

proof.text: Restrict the degree-zero additive equivalence to ker(1-T), with its inverse restricting by injectivity. In degree minus one equivariance and additivity identify the image subgroups of 1-T: e(x-Tx)=e(x)-T(e(x)), and surjectivity gives the reverse inclusion. QuotientAddGroup.congr induces the required additive quotient equivalence, with the stated formula on every representative.

proof.text: The left connecting square follows on quotient representatives by the left clause of Compatible followed by boundary naturality with identity precomposition and postcomposition by d. Use transport followed by U(d) equals outerMap and descend by quotient induction. The right square follows by the forgetting clause of Compatible and naturality of the inverse zero-shift isomorphism. Both squares concern all native morphisms.

proof.text: Apply the two assumed exact sequences to (K,H) and (J(K),L). For the native middle map m, injectivity follows as follows: if m(x)=0, the right square and the injective invariant equivalence give q(x)=0; exactness gives x=i(v); the left square and injectivity of the target boundary and coinvariant equivalence force v=0. For surjectivity, lift the invariant image of y through the invariant equivalence and the source surjective q to obtain x. The difference y-m(x) has zero invariant image, hence equals the target boundary of v; correct x by the source boundary of the inverse coinvariant image of v. This proves the short five lemma directly on the underlying additive groups with independent universes. Functoriality J.map_comp and associativity give naturality. Retain the specified outer equivalences and squares as witnesses in Represents.
